title: How Shall I Praise Th' Eternal God
description: How Shall I Praise Th' Eternal God in Tonic Solfa to CAITHNESS, doh is D: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 8 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for his Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707), Book II, composed on divine subjects, hymn 166, headed “The divine perfections”.
Watts' hymns were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Common Metre (8.6.8.6). This page sets the words to CAITHNESS; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: How shall I praise th'e-ter-nal God, That in-fin-ite un-known? Who can as-cend his high a-bode, Or ven-ture near his throne?

lines: How shall I praise th' eternal God,
Who can ascend his high abode,
Those watchful eyes that never sleep
His wisdom is a boundless deep
Where all our thoughts are drown'd.
Speak we of strength? His arm is strong
He knows no shadow of a change,
Firm as a rock his truth remains
While Mercy sends her pardons down,
Now to my soul, immortal King,
Then 't will be double joy to sing

source: Isaac Watts, Hymns and Spiritual Songs (1707)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to CAITHNESS by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
